A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COSMOS and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Content can be matched despite relocated references and reorganized supplementary sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original COSMOS experiments on retrieval, classification, segmentation and compositional understanding, alongside component and loss-scaling ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds LLaVA evaluations, text-cropping experiments and further empirical comparisons.

M1.justification: The architecture, cropping strategy, EMA teacher, losses and inference procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 now explicitly combines global and local student embeddings, aligning the pseudocode with the all-crop distillation procedure already described in v1 Section 3.3.

E1.justification: Section E.6 adds LLaVA evaluation on ScienceQA, POPE, GQA, TextVQA and MMMU, extending coverage to multimodal question answering, reasoning and hallucination assessment. Earlier coverage, including PixelProse and Winoground, remains.

E2.justification: Table 19 adds VeCLIP and MobileCLIP-B to retrieval comparisons. Table 18 adds SigLIP and DreamLIP to segmentation comparisons under Merged-30M training, while Table 14 introduces CLIP controls into the efficiency experiment.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce LLaVA feature-alignment pre-training and instruction tuning, alternative caption-cropping protocols including 15% token masking, and CLIP crop-count controls. Table 6 also revises the reported CC3M sample count from 2,818,104 to 2,823,019 and the Merged-30M total; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 17 tests independent sentence cropping against masked, summarized and local-within-global alternatives. Expanded Table 14 examines COSMOS cost and accuracy relative to CLIP with corresponding crop configurations. Existing component and SILC loss-scaling ablations remain; v1 Table 16 becomes v2 Table 20.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Expanded Table 14 and new Tables 16-19 add substantial results, including LLaVA ScienceQA scores of 67.8 for COSMOS versus 65.2 for CLIP. Main benchmark tables retain their scores. Section 4.1 nevertheless changes SigLIP's quoted Flickr30K text-to-image score from 73.6 to 73.3 without a corresponding Table 1 change.

T1.justification: The cross-attention definitions, loss formulations in Equations 1-7 and EMA update are retained. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: text cropping, cross-modality self-distillation, and improved fine-grained and compositional representations. The added experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section C.3 changes the explanation for harmful local image crops from overfitting to image-text misalignment. New sections explain conceptual correspondences, teacher overhead and DreamLIP's segmentation weakness. The explicit synthetic-caption hallucination limitation disappears, and the earlier memory/scaling caveat gives way to a more favorable overhead discussion.

D1.justification: v2 states that code is available, replacing v1's promise to release code and models. It corrects the distillation pseudocode and supplies implementation descriptions for the new cropping variants and LLaVA training stages. Core hyperparameters and hardware information remain.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, covering the five new evaluation benchmarks, VeCLIP, MobileCLIP and CoCa. Supplementary discussion expands positioning against caption-augmentation methods, while the main related-work framing around CLIP and self-supervised learning remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, terminology and affiliation edits. References move before the supplement, appendix experiments are reordered and extended, and the conclusion heading loses 'and Limitations'. Most existing narrative structure and prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The result presentation expands substantially through four new tables covering LLaVA, cropping strategies, matched-data segmentation and additional retrieval comparators. Table 14 gains CLIP rows and explicit method labels. Existing figures remain, and the SILC loss-scaling table is relocated and renumbered as Table 20.

improvement.justification: New cropping controls, CLIP cost comparisons and matched-data segmentation strengthen support for the design choices, while LLaVA adds useful transfer validation and the pseudocode correction improves reproducibility. These gains are tempered by the deleted hallucination caveat and overbroad SOTA discussion: Table 19 gives MobileCLIP-B higher MSCOCO image-to-text recall than COSMOS, 68.8 versus 68.0.
